prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in League City, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1144; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision in League City, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just be identified as the claimant on this one, if that's okay.

Q: That works. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was stopped at a traffic light on a main road, heading toward the shopping center. Traffic had been moving slowly, so I'd already come to a full stop.

Q: What happened next?

A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from behind, and my head snapped forward and back. My seatbelt locked up and I was thrown against it.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle right away?

A: I sat for a minute because I was dizzy. Then I got out and talked to the other driver. He said he had looked down at his phone for a second.

Q: Were you able to drive your car from the scene?

A: No, the rear bumper was damaged and the trunk wouldn't close properly, so a tow truck took it.

Q: Have you sought medical care since the collision?

A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. They diagnosed a neck strain and a lower back strain. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since then.

Q: How are your symptoms today?

A: My neck is stiff, especially when I turn to check my blind spots, and my lower back aches after sitting for more than about thirty minutes. Some days are better than others.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Just that I've been missing some time at work because of the pain, and I want my doctor's records to be part of this file.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
